Two years ago, Sonos ventured from wireless speakers into the over-ear headphone space. Now, Sonos appears poised to release a more premium successor with added AI features.

Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones are on the way

Chris Welch reports for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, a higher-end follow-up to its 2024 Ace headphones.

An application filed with the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC), discovered on Monday, reveals the product name and indicates up to five colour options, a richer palette than the original model's black and white.

Sonos is planning a product launch event in September, and the timing of this filing suggests the Ace Ultra will likely make its debut at that event.

The filing also contains technical clues suggesting the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Conrad has acknowledged that the original headphones launched without sufficient whole-home integration and failed to break through in a competitive market.

This time, Sonos appears to be tying its hardware more directly to its broader AI ambitions.

Conrad has described the company's opportunity as conversational computing and predictive intelligence in the home environment, delivered through Sonos hardware that operates across rooms and understands the habits of household members.

The company has already extended its Sonos Voice Control to operate smart home systems such as Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched this March, featuring the H2 chip, stronger noise cancellation and live translation. Siri AI will also extend to AirPods via iOS 27.

For more on the upcoming Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones, read the full Bloomberg report here.
